explanation: Fires on tokens inside formulaic, pattern-repeating structures where the token is predictable from an earlier parallel element: URL path segments after a slash (/wiki, /master, www), the second number in 'N X and M Y' counts (space before the number), digits in chemical formulas (Bi2Te3, As4Se3, 2,4,6-), and repeated list items or keys (<li>, =P(Z)). Weak, scattered firing on ordinary prose words. The examples share no single clear concept.

Fires on the name of a function or method being defined or declared, on its last subword or on the opening parenthesis right after it (handleAuth[Click](, filter[Module](, equals(, onDate[Set](, F[(]0), a(l)). Fires most strongly in code definitions and math function notation, and weakly on calls or on anonymous 'function(' arguments. It does not fire in ordinary prose.

Fires on the near-deterministic next token of a fixed, boilerplate multi-token sequence, mostly in code and licence text: '<?php', 'package org', '</script>', '<script type', '<span class', 'java.util.Objects', 'LIMITED TO', and also completions of word pieces in common technical words (st-en-osis, Ox-id-ative). It is much weaker on ordinary function words in prose.

Has two jobs. (1) Digits at the start of, or inside, structured numbers, especially docket numbers ('No. 02-17'), year digits ('20[1]9', '19[9]3') and leading zeros in decimals. (2) The newline right after an opening brace, bracket or tag in nested JSON, XML or HTML ('"f": {⏎', '<div ...">⏎'). It is weak on other tokens.

Fires diffusely on content and function words in formal academic, scientific or medical prose, notably institutional affiliation phrases ('Department [of]', 'Medical [University]', 'local [hospital]', 'National [Guard]') and abstract-style verbs and adjectives ('investigated', 'ensure', 'dominant'). There is no sharp token-level rule beyond an academic or institutional register.

Fires on word pieces in the middle of words and on function words in non-English text, especially Scandinavian ('til [å]', 'naturlig[vis]', 'ikke [kunne]'), plus Czech and Spanish. It also fires on internal subword fragments of rare technical or medical words (seborrheic [ker]atoses, gly[cop]roteins, d[ipy]ridamole, [den]ervated). There are miscellaneous other hits (XML quote, CWE number).

Fires on the token just before a categorical or enumerated label, such as a side, group, part or phase: the preposition or article in comparisons and locations ('predominance on [the] left', 'greatest [in] the ... groups', 'larger [in] UVL patients') and the label word or space before a number ('[Side] A', '([Part] 2)', '([phase] 2)', '[Group] 1', 'Division[ ]2', 'jogador[ ]2'). It is weak on generic prepositions without that contrastive or labelling context.

Fires on the token that continues or completes a multi-token technical term or identifier: package and module names in code (org.activ[iti], from [pyramid].config, 'd[va]/fetch', [Products].ERP5Form) and academic or statistical jargon split into pieces (nonparam[etric], proport[ional], self-e[ffic]acy, person[-years], short [form], Pl[aint]iff). It is weak on everyday words.

Fires on function words and punctuation in technical prose (code comments, docs, StackOverflow questions) that directly follow a mention of a data structure or code object and lead into its name or location: 'values [in] `array`', 'two dataframes[,] dfA', 'a dataframe [called] KeyRow', 'stored [in] ...', 'a table[,] BMST'. It is weaker on other connective words in programming prose and absent in non-technical text.

Fires most clearly on the word 'penalty'/'penalties' in any sense (death penalty, penalty shootout, administrative penalty, penalty points). It also fires strongly on a scattered set of unrelated tokens (compensating, Submerged, Worklight, Grand Valley, messing, compactness, safe zone) that share no evident theme.

Fires on the space token or first digit that begins a number in a quantity, duration or sequence expression, especially after 'every', 'for', 'within', 'up to', 'to', or as a later item in a list of numbers or time points ('0, 30,[ ]60', 'every[ ]50 d', 'for[ ]48 h', '1, 10, 100, [1]000'). It is weaker on digits in years, version numbers and dates.
